clue.text: One's willing to acquire new extra handle

indicators.note: to acquire something is to take it in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: one is the article a
game for anything means willing
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone eager to pick up a new nickname on top of the one they have.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of One's stands for 'has', joining A and the willing word; N goes in after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: An agname is an additional name or nickname, and handle is slang for a name.

clue.text: One special philosopher showing suspicion

clue.text: One acting Chief Inspector on TV irritates

explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to annoy or provoke them, from the stinging weed.

clue.text: Digger from zone in part of Galilee picked up

explanation.walkthrough: Digger is the nickname for an Australian soldier, and an Anzac was a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Anzac names a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand corps, which a digger typically was.

clue.text: Seaweed coming from rising loch froth in Scotland

clue.text: Food from the east, possibly just a trifle oriental mister rejected

clue.text: One is tense engaging acting medic, foot specialist

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: An iambist writes in iambs, and an iamb is a metrical foot, so the poet specialises in a foot.
